findings.title: Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.evidence: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached.

extra.solution: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.evidence: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files.

extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: Cross-Domain Misconfiguration
findings.evidence: Web browser data loading may be possible, due to a Cross Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration on the web server.

extra.solution:

findings.title: Retrieved from Cache
findings.evidence: The content was retrieved from a shared cache. If the response data is sensitive, personal or user-specific, this may result in sensitive information being leaked. In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.

extra.solution:
Validate that the response does not contain sensitive, personal or user-specific information. If it does, consider the use of the following HTTP response headers, to limit, or prevent the content being stored and retrieved from the cache by another user:
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private
Pragma: no-cache
Expires: 0
This configuration directs both HTTP 1.0 and HTTP 1.1 compliant caching servers to not store the response, and to not retrieve the response (without validation) from the cache, in response to a similar request.

correlate.executive_summary: The assessment found multiple web hardening issues and at least one high-risk information exposure. An unauthenticated directory listing at /ftp exposes numerous files (backups, encrypted artifacts, credential-like files) and is confirmed by both passive reconnaissance and active scanning. Several HTTP security headers are missing (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) and cache-control behavior should be reviewed; a possible CORS misconfiguration was also flagged. No product/version CVE matches were available from service/version data, so findings are based on observed configuration and content only.

findings.title: Exposed directory listing and sensitive files under /ftp
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 200 on /ftp (response differs from baseline 404; body sha256 noted). va (zap): crawl shows many /ftp files (e.g. encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, package.json.bak, juicy_malware_*.url) and serve-index references in application routes, indicating an actual directory listing and publicly accessible files.

findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) header not set
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set' flagged across many endpoints (confirmed). recon: manual header check also recorded missing content-security-policy on root response.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header not set
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set' flagged on many endpoints (confirmed). recon: also recorded missing strict-transport-security in header checks.

findings.title: Cross-Domain (CORS) misconfiguration
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Cross-Domain Misconfiguration' reported across many endpoints indicating CORS policy may allow unsafe cross-origin access. No additional agent validated exact Access-Control-Allow-Origin behavior, so this remains a suspected configuration issue.

findings.title: Missing X-Frame-Options header (anti-clickjacking)
findings.evidence: va (nikto): 'The anti-clickjacking X-Frame-Options header is not present.' (nikto GET http://juiceshop.cortexlab.org.in:443/). No corroborating agent explicitly validated header across other endpoints.

findings.title: Cache-control directives require review; content retrieved from shared cache
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Re-examine Cache-control Directives' flagged for multiple endpoints and 'Retrieved from Cache' observed for /robots.txt. These indicate missing/incorrect cache-control headers or shared cache behavior; no proof of sensitive-data leakage was obtained during testing.

findings.title: Cloudflare CDN detected (cf-ray header present)
findings.evidence: recon: technology fingerprint detected 'cloudflare'. va (nikto): 'Uncommon header "cf-ray" found'. Together these indicate the service sits behind Cloudflare (informational).

findings.title: Modern web application fingerprint (informational)
